- **`spec-kitty implement` no longer refuses to allocate a lane when a mission's `status.json` has drifted, and `spec-kitty merge` no longer blocks a legitimate integration on the same drift** (#5160 friction 1, #4955). **Before:** `status.json` is a derived snapshot of the append-only `status.events.jsonl` (the sole authority), but both the lane allocator and the mission→target squash git-merged the snapshot; when it diverged on both sides the event log union-merged cleanly yet the snapshot conflicted, so allocation failed with "cannot auto-merge the recorded planning commit / dependency lane" and integration failed closed — a hard stop on a routine, safe divergence an operator could not fix. **After:** when the only remaining conflict is a derived `status.json`, both paths regenerate it from the union-merged event log (one shared authority, `status.reconcile_status_snapshot`) and complete the merge. A genuine conflict in human-authored content (a `tasks/WP*.md`, source file, …) still fails closed — the regeneration never green-washes real divergence, and it also fails closed when there is no event log to derive from. Red-first regressions at both seams. This lands the `status.json` reconciliation; the remaining #4955 reconciliation classes — union drivers for `mission-events.jsonl` and `kitty-ops/lifecycle.jsonl`, and the `decisions/index.json` re-fold — are deferred to the dedicated design pass #4955 calls for (they require a new governed merge-driver classification and a C-006 completeness-guard decision). Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **`spec-kitty agent context resolve --action tasks` (and the other planning actions) now report the same `feature_dir` as `check-prerequisites`, so tasks author where `finalize-tasks` reads** (#5160 friction 3; #2017/#2101 recurrence). **Before:** on a coordination-topology mission `context resolve` returned the coordination-worktree directory while `check-prerequisites` and `finalize-tasks` anchored to the primary checkout, so an agent authoring at the reported path wrote to the coord surface while finalize parsed an empty primary `tasks/` — a silent split. **After:** planning/authoring actions (`specify`, `plan`, `tasks`, `tasks_outline`, `tasks_packages`, `tasks_finalize`) primary-anchor the reported `feature_dir` through the same authority `check-prerequisites` uses; status-reading actions (`status`, `analyze`, `accept`) keep the coordination read surface unchanged. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **`make test-fast` / `make test-full` run from inside a lane worktree no longer false-red with `ModuleNotFoundError: pytestarch`** (#5160 friction 2). **Before:** `pytestarch` was declared only in the `test` optional extra, but the make targets run `uv run --frozen pytest`, which in a fresh lane worktree provisions only the default dependency groups — so architectural-style tests failed for a missing dependency rather than a real regression. **After:** `pytestarch` is mirrored into the `[dependency-groups].dev` group (as `pytest-xdist` and `pytest-timeout` already were), and a packaging-shape guard fails closed if any plugin the make targets need without `--all-extras` is ever dropped from the dev group.
- **The error shown when a coordination worktree is not yet materialized now names a command that actually creates it** (#5113, remedy text). **Before:** `CoordinationWorktreeUnmaterialized` advertised `spec-kitty doctor workspaces --fix` (which only removes stale registrations and cannot create a worktree) and promised a self-materialization that does not always happen, sending operators toward a no-op. **After:** the message names the concrete `git -C <repo> worktree add <coord-worktree> <coord-branch>` command (both the local-branch and remote-only recovery paths), and notes that `--fix` cannot create the worktree.
- **`make test-fast` is green again from the isolated linked worktrees the contributor workflow mandates** (#4873). **Before:** three charter JSON error-contract tests probed the real process cwd through the charter write-root guard, which fires from a linked worktree before the tests' mocked conditions run, so the mandatory fast baseline showed three unrelated failures that obscured change-specific regressions. **After:** the tests adopt the canonical cwd-isolation fixture, so they assert their intended contracts from any working directory (no production behavior changed — the write-root guard invariant is preserved).
- **`spec-kitty upgrade` no longer crashes on a legacy mission whose `meta.json` is not a JSON object or not valid UTF-8** (#2479; with #2477, #2478, #4362, #5135). **Before:** the 0.13.8 `target_branch` migration read each mission's `meta.json` with a bare `json.loads`, so a `meta.json` holding a JSON array or scalar was flagged as needing the migration and then aborted `upgrade` with a `TypeError`, and a non-UTF-8 `meta.json` aborted detection with a `UnicodeDecodeError`. **After:** the 0.13.0, 0.13.5 and 0.13.8 migrations read `meta.json` through the canonical reader: detection skips a malformed file, and the 0.13.8 upgrade reports it per mission (`Malformed JSON in <mission>/meta.json: …`) instead of crashing. The internal architecture gates guarding these reads now fail closed on a source file they cannot parse instead of silently skipping it.
- **`spec-kitty doctor coordination --fix` (and the coord read path) no longer flatten a live coordination mission when run from a checkout that cannot see the remote coordination branch — a `--single-branch`/`--depth 1`/CI clone or a pruned-origin ref — so a teammate following the CLI's own hints can no longer hide the whole team's approvals** (#4979, P0). **Before:** the single canonical branch-existence probe `_coord_branch_exists` decided "coordination branch never-created/deleted" from only the local head plus already-fetched `refs/remotes/*` refs (the #2614 residual). A single-branch/shallow/CI clone, or a normal clone after origin's coord branch was pruned, has neither ref although the branch still exists on origin — so the probe reported "absent", `agent status emit` refused with the deleted-branch error and steered the operator to `doctor coordination --fix`, which flattened `meta.json` (dropped `coordination_branch`, demoted `topology: coord → lanes`); `implement`'s planning-artifact auto-commit then carried the flattened `meta.json` to the target branch, and on an ordinary pull every teammate's mission flattened — approved WPs read `planned`, dependents were refused, `doctor` reported healthy, exit 0, no shipped command un-flattened. **After** (three-tier, fail-closed): (1) the probe now consults the remote authority via one shared tri-state `remote_branch_lookup` primitive — a `git ls-remote` HIT ⇒ present; a reachable clean-miss across all remotes ⇒ absent; an unreachable/timing-out/erroring remote ⇒ fail-closed present (bounded timeout, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` + SSH `BatchMode`, memoized) — and **zero remotes configured retains today's local-authority "absent"**, so a genuinely-deleted branch in an origin-less repo still flattens; the network probe runs only after the local-head and `refs/remotes/` fast paths miss, and the pre-existing `_branch_resolvable` duplicate is unified onto the same primitive (its own missing-timeout hang fixed too). (2) `doctor coordination --fix` re-verifies the branch against the remote before the destructive flatten, refusing (meta.json untouched, actionable "run `git fetch`" message) when it still exists on any remote. (3) `implement`'s planning-artifact auto-commit now REFUSES, rather than silently commits, a `meta.json` diff that drops `coordination_branch` (a topology demotion) — the demotion check reads meta.json through the canonical `kernel.meta_decode` L1 decoder (single meta-decode authority), while a legitimate first commit or an ordinary non-demoting edit is unaffected. A remote-only checkout's coord read now raises `CoordinationWorktreeUnmaterialized` with fetch-first guidance, never silently substituting the empty primary surface. Red-first `@pytest.mark.regression` reproductions per tier through the real production seams. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **`CI Fleet Verdict → identify` runs again on every `main` push instead of crashing at startup** (#5127; closes #5000). **Before:** `ci-fleet-verdict.yml` invokes `scripts/ci/fleet_verdict.py` as a bare script (`python3 scripts/ci/fleet_verdict.py`), so `sys.path[0]` was `scripts/ci/` rather than the repo root, and the script's module-level `from scripts.ci.reconcile_retry import retry_with_backoff` raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'` on every run — no fleet verdict had been produced for `main` since the reconcile-retry change (#4882 / `50777e5fc`). **After:** the script inserts the repo root on `sys.path` before that import (the same guard already used by `scripts/ci/stale_running_sweep.py`), and a new regression guard (`tests/ci/test_workflow_script_import_guard.py`) derives every bare-invoked workflow script from the workflow YAML, keeps the ones whose module-level code imports `scripts.*`, and runs each the way CI does (by path, `PYTHONPATH` unset, from an isolated cwd) asserting the import never raises — so the whole defect class, not just this one script, fails a test before it can red `main`. Internal CI only; no shipped surface or CLI version change.
- **The DEFAULT `spec-kitty merge` no longer false-FAILs a legitimate squash when two approved work packages edit *disjoint regions of the same file* — the clean 3-way-merged result now lands instead of the whole merge being reverted (#5051-adjacent clean case; Epic #5001 follow-up, complements the #5038 projection-axis fix).** The squash content proof (`reconciliation.py::_unattributable_content_squash`) attributes every result blob to approved work; it rejected a legitimate blob that equalled *neither* single approved parent. **Before:** when two approved lanes edited disjoint hunks of one file, the squash's clean auto-merged blob was authored by neither lane, so it was judged "un-attributable" and the target was compare-and-swap-reverted — a fully-approved mission could not complete on the default path. **After:** a path touched by **exactly two** approved lanes is attributed when — and only when — `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two lanes' commits clean-merges to *exactly* the target blob (git derives the merge base itself and honors `.gitattributes`); everything unsound fails closed (>2 approved lanes, a binary file, an unresolvable base, a genuine conflict, or git < 2.38 all stay FAIL, never attribute). The recognizer also guards its two merge inputs against a merge-commit lane tip that smuggled a disjoint second-parent hunk into the shared path (the #4977 carrier mechanism): it refuses to simulate unless each contributing lane's tip-tree blob at the path equals that lane's vetted first-parent-authored blob, so removed/canceled/smuggled/superseded content can never be folded into the attributed result and still FAILs — the #4945/#4977/#4981 canceled-content data-loss guarantees and the superseded-`v1` guardian hold. This is the blob-**attribution** axis counterpart to the #5038 coord-bookkeeping-**projection** driver-replay fix (the projection axis is upstream's; this closes the *product-path* clean-3-way case the attribution axis left un-attributed). Real-CLI red-first reproduction: `tests/terminus/test_repro_5051_clean_3way.py`. Residual tracked follow-up (honest `xfail(strict)`, not green-washed): a genuine *same-line* conflict resolved to a manually-authored third blob is reconstructable by no deterministic function, so it stays un-attributable and is tracked in **#5051**. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **`spec-kitty implement` no longer silently strands committed work by re-cutting a deleted lane, and the second work package on a coordination-topology mission can now start** (#4889, #4905). **Before:** (#4889) when a work package's lane worktree AND lane branch were both gone while the WP was still in a non-terminal state, re-running `implement` fell through `allocate_lane_worktree`'s FRESH route (which consulted no WP lane state), silently cut a new empty lane from the coordination tip, printed `✓ Lane worktree ready`, exited 0, and overwrote the persisted lane metadata — the committed WP work was left unreachable while canonical status still said in-progress, and a later `merge` landed the empty lane. (#4905) on `coord`/`lanes_with_coord` topologies the agent-verb lifecycle commit staged the PRIMARY-partition `kitty-specs/<slug>/tasks/WP*.md` onto the coordination branch, so every later lane's FR-009 planning-artifact merge hit an add/add conflict (`PlanningCommitMergeConflictError`) and the second work package could not start. **After:** (#4889) a fail-closed pre-flight inside `allocate_lane_worktree` — covering both the CLI (`create_lane_workspace`) and the orchestrator-api caller (`_resolve_start_workspace`) — distinguishes a destroyed lane (persisted `WorkspaceContext` + non-terminal coord-surface status + both refs gone + the cut-from base not yet on the target) from a genuinely new one and refuses with a `DestroyedLaneError` naming the missing branch and a recovery ref instead of re-cutting; the intact-lane resume paths (REUSE / CRASH_RECOVERY) and a legitimate re-open (tip already on target) are unchanged. (#4905) the shared coordination-commit sink now partitions staged paths by artifact kind, routing PRIMARY-partition work-package files to the primary target via `commit_to_primary_target` and keeping the coordination branch free of `tasks/WP*.md` at all three lifecycle staging sites (claim / resume-refresh / review-claim), so the next lane's planning merge no longer conflicts. Red-first `@pytest.mark.regression` reproductions across both allocator callers, all three allocation routes, and all three coord staging sites. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump. Known follow-up: the #4889 REACH check uses the persisted cut-from base as a proxy for the lane work tip (fail-closed for the coord P0; a narrow non-coord false-pass window remains until the lane work tip is persisted).

- **`spec-kitty merge` (fresh or `--resume`) no longer refuses a legitimate Mission whose lanes were created under one naming form while its lanes manifest records a Mission identity that yields a different one** (#5108). **Before:** six read sites (the reconciliation claim, pre-interrupt lane-tip capture, the pre-mutation safety preflight, cleanup's residue scan, the `lifecycle_sync` multi-candidate probe, and acceptance's lane source-root resolution) re-derived a lane's branch/worktree name using the lanes manifest's Mission identity, instead of reusing the name lane *creation* actually produced from the slug and lane id. A legacy `NNN-slug` Mission whose identity was backfilled after its lanes existed, a slug embedding a mismatched mid8, or an invalid manifest identity (≥ 8 or < 8 characters) each merged into "no approved lane resolved any commits" — or crashed outright on the < 8 character shape. **After:** every merge stage resolves the lane branch and worktree that were actually created (ADR `docs/adr/3.x/2026-09-26-2-lane-naming-keyed-on-creation-input.md`); all four divergent shapes merge cleanly, cleanup leaves no orphaned branch or worktree, and an approved non-canceled lane whose created branch does not exist in git now REFUSEs naming that branch instead of silently producing an empty commit set.
- **A freshly created coordination-topology Mission's decision ledger no longer partially writes and fails, and `doctor coordination --fix` now actually applies the remedy it advertises** (#5113). **Before:** on a Mission with a coordination branch present but its coordination worktree not yet materialized, `decision open`/`resolve`/`defer`/`cancel` could partially write the decision ledger and then fail because the coordination worktree was absent — and the remedy the error advertised did not actually materialize it. **After:** each verb materializes the coordination worktree (via the existing materialization path) before any write, and fails with nothing written only when materialization itself fails; `spec-kitty doctor coordination --mission <slug> --fix` now materializes a missing coordination worktree and is the remedy the unmaterialized-coordination error names.
- **Re-finalizing tasks on a Mission whose identity was backfilled after its lanes were created no longer retargets `implement`/`merge` at a Mission branch that was never created** (FR-011). **Before:** `finalize-tasks` recomputed the lanes manifest's `mission_branch` from the current Mission identity every time it ran, so backfilling a legacy Mission's identity and then re-finalizing silently rewrote the recorded Mission branch to a name creation never produced. **After:** only the *first* `finalize-tasks` for a Mission defines its recorded Mission branch; every later re-finalize preserves it byte-identically, and any remaining fallback that would recompose it from an invalid identity now refuses with a typed error (`LaneComputationError` / `BranchIdentityUnresolved`) naming `spec-kitty migrate backfill-identity` as the remedy, rather than crashing.
- **`spec-kitty charter context` now prints doctrine text verbatim instead of letting Rich eat bracketed tokens** (#5061). **Before:** `--include tactic:<id>` and the action body were printed as Rich markup, so tokens such as `[build]` were silently stripped from the output. **Now:** both body paths print with markup disabled.
- **Every `charter` command error message now shows bracketed tokens verbatim instead of having Rich silently eat them** (#5130; error-path twin of #5061). **Before:** the shared `_emit_error` helper interpolated the message straight into a `[red]…[/red]` Rich markup string, so any error echoing a bracketed selector or doctrine label (for example an unresolved `[build]` token, across all 8 charter subcommands) was mangled. **Now:** the message is passed through `rich.markup.escape`, while the intended red label stays styled — so the whole charter CLI error surface is fixed, not just the one command.
- **Concurrent spec-kitty commands no longer crash at startup on a fresh machine or CI runner (#3998).** **Before:** on a cold, shared Spec Kitty home, commands that ran startup asset preparation at the same moment (a new CI runner, a new machine, an orchestrator starting several agents) intermittently crashed with a traceback: `RuntimeError: Asset changed during preparation: …`. It happened to 1–5 of 16–32 processes. The losing processes read a peer's half-written install, re-raced it three times without waiting, then aborted. **After:** such a read now waits for the installing peer and re-checks once under that peer's own lock. The command then runs normally. A warm start is unchanged: lock-free, one check. Source-asset drift is still refused. When startup preparation genuinely cannot complete, the command prints one `Error:` line (or a JSON error object with `--json`) and exits 1, with no traceback. Also closes the stale #4017, which PR #4174 fixed but never linked.
- **`spec-kitty merge --strategy merge --resume` no longer strands the merge — or, on the "Commit" mis-remedy, loses the whole mission's code — when the primary checkout lags its own HEAD after an interrupted terminus** (#4997; primary-checkout sibling of the closed #4982). **Before:** after `merge` advanced the target ref with `git update-ref` but the following `git reset --hard` that refreshes the primary checkout failed (an `index.lock` held by an IDE or another git process) or the process was killed, the primary checkout's index/tree lagged its own already-advanced HEAD and the mission's integrated files read as staged deletions. `merge --resume` then refused `MERGE_UNSAFE_PRIMARY_DIRTY` and advised "Commit, stash, or revert" — so the merge was stranded, and an operator (or an agent following the literal remedy) who committed the staged deletions recorded a commit deleting every mission file; the resumed `git merge` was "Already up to date" (the mission branch was already an ancestor), yet under the merge strategy the FR-037 zero-diff adjudication never fired (`_merge_branch_into` reported the no-op as `already_applied=False`), so every WP was stamped `done`, lanes and the mission branch were deleted, exit 0 — the target left with none of the mission's code. **After:** on a `--resume`, a `MERGE_UNSAFE_PRIMARY_DIRTY` refusal that is a *provably pure* behind-own-HEAD lag is recovered in place (`git reset --hard HEAD`) and the merge continues, so the approved code lands. Recovery is gated on both lane-ancestry (`BEHIND_OWN_HEAD`) **and** a phantom-only content proof — the primary's working tree AND index must be byte-identical to the persisted `pre_mutation_target_sha` and HEAD its descendant, and no untracked *or gitignored* file may obstruct a restored path — so a genuine coexisting edit, an intentional non-mission deletion, or an untracked/gitignored collision in the same window makes the resume REFUSE fail-closed, never resetting away real work. Separately, the MERGE-strategy "Already up to date" no-op is now reported as `changed=False` (→ `already_applied=True`), so the strategy-agnostic zero-diff guard (renamed `_reject_zero_diff_noop_integration`) adjudicates it exactly like the squash no-op — a no-op integration that would leave the target tree missing approved content refuses (non-zero) instead of reporting false success (lane→mission consolidation keeps its benign no-ops). Red-first, real-CLI reproductions: the previously-`xfail` `tests/terminus/test_repro_4997.py` now models the real behind-own-HEAD window and passes; a phantom-only safety test proves a genuine edit and an untracked collision both survive; unit tests pin the merge no-op adjudication. Closes the #4997 residual that the #5001 terminus-integrity epic tracked as an open follow-up.
- **`spec-kitty merge`'s DEFAULT squash no longer false-REFUSEs a legitimate merge when a coord-bookkeeping file (e.g. a mission tracer under `traces/*.md`) was edited on both the target and an approved lane from a shared baseline** (#5038). **Before:** the squash coord-bookkeeping-projection proof (`_assert_squash_projected_content_landed` / `projected_content_matches_target`) demanded raw `coord_bytes == target_bytes` for every projected path — but the path's registered `spec-kitty merge-driver-*` (e.g. `merge-driver-traces`, a deterministic, lossless, order-preserving union) legitimately resolves that overlap to a THIRD blob (neither parent verbatim), so the byte-equality proof REFUSEd a clean, non-resumed, single-approved-lane merge with exit 1 and no teardown — a real trigger for any mission that edits a tracer/verdict/notes file on both target and lane during the merge window, not merely a theoretical edge case. **After:** the proof replaces raw byte-equality with **driver-replay attribution**: for a path that diverged from the shared checkpoint baseline, it reconstructs the expected landed blob by replaying the path's registered driver, in-process, on `(checkpoint blob, pre-squash-target blob, coord blob)` — the SAME deterministic computation git invoked during the real squash — and PASSes iff the actual landed blob byte-equals that replay. The non-diverged subset keeps the original byte-equality proof verbatim (no regression), and the proof stays fail-closed: a diverged path with NO registered driver, a missing blob, or a driver error still REFUSEs, never passing vacuously. `test_5038_p1_...` (previously a documented, real `xfail`) now PASSes for real through the live `spec-kitty merge` CLI; `test_5038_p2_...` is RE-GROUNDED (operator ruling `DM-01M3EC2FMWKCKGSBX1QHC7GFCJ`) onto a landed blob the driver replay genuinely does NOT reproduce (content dropped, not merely present-but-diverged), since P1's and P2's ORIGINAL scenarios were informationally identical to the pre-fix proof and a sound fix necessarily flips both. The sibling attribution-axis 3-way residual — **#5021 residual-2** (`test_squash_three_way_merge_resolution_is_unattributable`, a stock-git conflict + manual resolution on a path with NO registered driver) — is a distinct, soundly-unfixable root and stays an honest, narrowed `xfail(strict=True)`; it is not touched or weakened by this fix. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **Terminus reconciliation attribution — the DEFAULT `spec-kitty merge` no longer silently drops a canceled WP's file deletion, and a mixed approved+canceled lane / a completed-but-interrupted squash no longer false-blocks a legitimate merge (Epic #5001 follow-ups #5022, #5018, #5021).** **Before:** (1) #5022 — the default-squash reconciliation content axis (`_unattributable_content_squash`) skipped deletions (`if status.startswith("D"): continue`), so a canceled/removed WP's deletion of a pre-existing file that no approved lane re-authors rode a carrier lane onto the target and landed at exit 0 — silent data loss on `main`. (2) #5018 — `_collect_excluded` attributed exclusion at LANE granularity: if any WP in a write-scope lane was canceled it added ALL of that lane's tip commits to the excluded set, colliding with the approved survivor's own commits (which `_collect_approved_shas` added too), so a legitimate `--strategy merge`/`rebase` of a lane holding both an approved and a canceled-with-provenance WP was wrongly FAILed and the target reverted. (3) #5021 r1 — a `merge --resume` that crashed mid-teardown rebuilt the reconciliation claim against a now-partial `authored_blobs` set (a torn-down lane branch yields empty first-parent authorship) and re-ran the content axis, false-REFUSing a squash merge that had already landed and PASSed. **After:** the squash content axis attributes DELETIONS too — a squashed deletion is legitimate only when an approved lane's first-parent authored history also deletes the path (new `ApprovedWpCommitSet.authored_deletions`, computed in one spine walk by `_final_authored_walk`) or the path is mission bookkeeping; an unattributable deletion FAILs and compare-and-swap-reverts the target, same as the add/modify path. `_collect_excluded` now subtracts the approved lanes' first-parent authored SHAs/patch-ids, so a mixed lane's survivor commits are attributed as approved authorship and not double-counted as excluded — while a canceled commit that is NOT on any approved first-parent spine (e.g. second-parent-smuggled) stays excluded and still FAILs when reachable (the #4977 data-loss guarantee is preserved; the fix corrects attribution granularity, never gate strictness). `merge --resume` records a `MergeState.reconciliation_passed_target_sha` compare-and-swap anchor the instant reconciliation PASSes, and on resume a completed-but-mid-teardown state (target already at that tip) finishes teardown without re-running the content axis against a partial claim — while a genuinely-incomplete resume still runs the full gate. Real-CLI red-first reproductions for each defect (`tests/terminus/test_repro_5022.py`, `test_repro_5018.py`, `test_repro_5021.py`). Residual tracked follow-up (honest `xfail(strict)`, not green-washed): **#5038** — the squash coord-bookkeeping-projection proof (`_assert_squash_projected_content_landed`) can false-REFUSE only on a genuine 3-way coord-partition content divergence (a path edited on both target and lane from a shared baseline → squash blob equals neither parent), which converges with the existing 3-way merge-resolution follow-up (a `test_repro_5038.py` P1 xfail documents the trigger; a P2 guard pins that a genuine failed projection still REFUSEs). Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **The planning-pin classifier now resolves the target-branch tip deterministically, so a tag sharing the target branch's name can no longer misclassify a lane's recorded planning commit — and two adjacent tasks-lifecycle nits are cleared** (#4857, #4593, #4152; Epic #4883). **Before (#4857):** the tip that `classify_recorded_pin` classifies against was captured by two separate helpers (`lanes/merge._rev_parse`, `mission_finalize._capture_target_branch_tip`) that both resolved the **bare** branch name; git resolves an ambiguous name (a tag colliding with the target branch) to the *tag*, so the pin could be classified against the tag's commit instead of the branch tip — while `merge/preflight.py` and `_coordination_doctor.py` already resolved `refs/heads/{target_branch}` and got the branch. (The original ticket's "the two helpers diverge on ambiguous refs" premise was disproved empirically — `rev-parse` and `rev-parse --verify` behave identically; the real defect was the shared bare-name resolution.) **After:** one canonical `capture_branch_tip` helper (`core/vcs/git.py`) resolves `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/{branch}` — deterministically the branch tip, never a same-named tag — with a single documented ambiguity/error contract (missing → `None`, never raises); all six classifier-tip callers route through it and `_capture_target_branch_tip` is deleted. A red-first branch/tag-collision regression pins the fix. **Also folded (same tasks→lanes→finalize blast radius):** the `move-task` behind-count no longer understates source divergence on merge-rich target branches — it counts commits reachable through TREESAME merges via `--full-history` (message-only, fail-open preserved; #4593 item 1); and the `finalize-tasks` dependency path drops a provably dead frontmatter-field guard (behaviour-preserving) while its cyclic-dependency test's exit-code assertion is made load-bearing — it now reads `typer.Exit.exit_code` instead of a non-existent `.code`, so it can actually catch a wrong `Exit(0)` (#4152 items 2 & 3). Dispositions recorded, not silently dropped: #4152 item 1 declined (conflicts with item 2 and would warn on the intended #4135 path); #4593 item 2 declined (body-form on a merged PR); #4611 dropped to its functional epic #4441.
- **Two more asset-preservation flows no longer silently delete or clobber operator-authored files — the `.kittify/` centralisation migration and the git-clone doctrine-pack fetch — and the data-loss class is now closed by construction for both** (#4961, #4960, #4989; extends epic #4792/#4915). Each mutating flow removed or overwrote user content on identity it could not actually prove, and the removal census did not yet scan either module. All fixes are ATDD red-first, and this is a bug-fix — **no CLI version bump**.
  - **The `.kittify/` centralisation migration no longer removes a shared asset that merely *differs* from the shipped default** (#4961). **Before:** `runtime/migrate.py` classified a shared asset that differed from its package counterpart as removable — but "differs" is content-indistinguishable between an outdated default and a genuine team customisation, so a hand-authored file could be deleted with no backup. **After:** every removal routes through `asset_preservation.guard_destructive_removal` with a `CanonicalContentProver`: the guard performs the delete **only** for a proven byte-identical (package-owned) file; any differing or unprovable file (`SUPERSEDED`) is preserved in place and reported honestly on the guard's verdict, not the optimistic classification. Byte-identity is the sole ownership signal at this site (`check_marker=False`), so a *differing* customisation that merely embeds the `spec-kitty-command-version` marker literal is preserved too, not deleted via the marker — closing the invariant by construction. The one residual raw literal is an empty-only `Path.rmdir` behind an `iterdir()` emptiness check.
  - **The git-clone doctrine-pack fetch no longer clobbers a pre-existing pack or silently discards local work on update** (#4960, #4989). **Before:** `doctrine/sources/git_source.py` could overwrite a non-empty `target_dir` (a hand-authored pack) on first install, and its update path ran `git reset --hard` that silently discarded uncommitted local changes or local commits ahead of the reset target. **After:** first install refuses a non-empty `target_dir` up front and clones into a `.tmp-<uuid>` sibling promoted onto the target via a move-aside (`.old-<uuid>`) pattern — a failed clone/checkout/promote removes **only** the temp/backup this run created, never the target (#4960); update fail-closed **refuses** the `reset --hard` when the working tree is dirty or carries commits ahead of the reset target, and resolves the reset target by ref type (`origin/<ref>` only for a real remote branch) rather than a blanket `origin/<ref>` that would regress tag/SHA-pinned packs (#4989).
  - **Closed by construction (FR-005):** the removal census (`tests/architectural/test_mutation_ownership_routing.py`, sharing plumbing with the git-op gate via `_destructive_op_census.py`) now scans both modules — `runtime/migrate.py` as a routed module (its fix-site carries no raw literal) and `git_source.py` as scanned-but-not-routed with a fail-closed guard that a user-content removal (e.g. `shutil.rmtree(target_dir)`) can never be allowlisted — and the git-argv gate's `reset --hard` allowlist entry is re-pinned to the fixed, dirty/ahead-guarded reset. Both gates are proven fail-able by self-mutation, so any future un-rationalised destructive literal in either module fails CI.
- **`spec-kitty accept` now fails closed when `lanes.json` is absent, instead of silently skipping the entire acceptance-matrix gate and recording acceptance on an unverified mission** (#4891, P0). **Before:** when `kitty-specs/<slug>/lanes.json` was absent, the lane-gate resolver (`_resolve_lanes_manifest_or_stop`) returned a bare `None` and `_check_lane_gates` bailed *before* running the branch gate and every acceptance-matrix check (presence / evidence / negative-invariant / verdict) — with no diagnostic on either output channel. `summary.ok` stayed `True`, the command exited `0`, and `perform_acceptance` wrote and committed `accepted_at` / `accept_commit` / `acceptance_history` into `meta.json` while every acceptance criterion was still `pending` (or the matrix did not exist). The same mission with `lanes.json` present was correctly refused; only genuine absence failed open — a deliberate "silent no-op" the resolver's own docstring justified. This was reachable through an ordinary path: upgrading a 3.2.0-era coordination mission leaves `lanes.json` absent on the primary partition, where `implement`/`review`/`merge` already fail closed but `accept` did not. **After:** absence routes through the canonical `require_lanes_json`, and its `MissingLanesError` is handled by the same fail-closed helper as `CorruptLanesError` — recording an `activity_issue` (so `AcceptanceSummary.ok` becomes `False`), a `blocked_checks` `lanes_manifest` diagnostic, and a `skipped_checks` entry for every acceptance-matrix gate that did not run (including the matrix-presence check). `spec-kitty accept` now exits non-zero, lists the skipped/blocked checks, points at the recovery (`finalize-tasks` / `doctor mission-state --fix`), and does **not** record or commit acceptance on an unverified matrix — consistent with `implement`/`review`/`merge`. `lanes.json` is a PRIMARY-partition artifact, so the read stays primary (no coord-aware read introduced — distinct from #3439); `merge`'s deliberate `--skip-lanes` opt-in is untouched. ATDD red-first, single-authority fix confined to the resolver seam.
- **A reviewer's rejection can no longer be silently overwritten by a concurrent stale approval — the review gate no longer ships rejected code — by adopting `spec-kitty-events` 10.4.0** (#4990; via spec-kitty/spec-kitty-events#69). **Before:** the CLI pinned `spec-kitty-events>=9,<10` (9.1.6), whose status-diary reducer was last-writer-wins by wall-clock `at`; two reviewers on one WP from two checkouts (reject `in_review -> planned`, then a later-`at` stale `in_review -> approved`) reduced to `approved` after an ordinary pull — `status validate` passed and `merge` shipped the rejected implementation, exit 0. **After:** the pin moves to `spec-kitty-events>=10.4.0,<11`, whose reducer arbitrates by from-lane continuity — a forward transition never overwrites an already-applied rollback unless it causally followed it — so the committed rejection wins regardless of timestamp; a genuine reject→rework→approve chain is unaffected. The CLI's `status.reducer`/`materialize` inherits the corrected precedence automatically (pinned by the packaged conformance golden `status-diary-replay-concurrent-reject-beats-approve`, now exercised through the CLI materialization parity test). This is the post-launch adoption **off the 9.1.6 launch train** (planning#2000): it crosses the events 9→10 major boundary — whose sole breaking change (10.0.0 rejects mixed ISO-8601 `occurred_at` spellings) does not affect the CLI, which always emits `datetime.isoformat()` — and activates the typed `WorkObservation` codec that landed in events 10.1.0 (`live_work` `codec_state()` → `typed`, emissions now model-validated).
- **`spec-kitty doctor mission-state --audit` no longer red-flags a mission whose snapshot differs from the reducer only in provenance attribution** (#4990). **Before:** adopting the `spec-kitty-events` 10.4.0 reducer (above) re-attributes per-work-package provenance (`actor` / `last_event_id` / `last_transition_at`) for missions carrying `verdict_provenance_backfill` migration events — **without changing any lane or outcome** — so an archived mission's committed `status.json`, materialized under the old reducer, now differs from the new reducer output and raised a hard `SNAPSHOT_DRIFT` TeamSpace-blocker (for a non-terminal mission the archive gate forbids editing, this red'd the corpus audit unfixably). **After:** when the drift is confined to that provenance triple — identical work-package membership and byte-identical lanes, counts, summary, and every other field — the audit reports a non-blocking `SNAPSHOT_DRIFT_PROVENANCE` **warning** instead of the blocking error. Any drift touching a lane, count, or other field still raises the hard `SNAPSHOT_DRIFT` error (so a genuine #4990 concurrent-reject *outcome* correction, which is a lane change, is never masked). Complements the #4690 terminal-drift tolerance.
- **The autonomous `spec-kitty next --result success` loop no longer spins forever on a rejected review or wedges at exit 1 on the default `coord` topology — it now derives the next step/WP from the same coord-aware finalized-task-board authority query mode already uses** (mission `advancing-next-board-unification-01M3BGQ0`; `#4980`, `#4975`). **Before:** after a review REJECT (`move-task <wp> --to planned`), every later `next --result success` returned `kind=step action=review wp_id=null` — a WP-less "Run `spec-kitty next` to advance" composition placeholder, exit 0, forever, because `_state_to_action("review", ...)` found no `for_review` WP and fell through to generic template resolution instead of re-checking the board (#4980). Separately, on the default `coord`/`lanes_with_coord` topology, advancing `next` reaching the `implement` step returned `kind=blocked reason="No action mapped for WP step 'implement'"`, exit 1, because the advancing path resolved WP lanes off the coord-aware runtime `feature_dir` — which carries no `tasks/` under coord topology (a PRIMARY-partition artifact) — instead of the coord-aware `status_dir` paired with the PRIMARY task-board dir (#4975), while query mode and `orchestrator-api list-ready` both correctly reported the WP ready. **After:** both WP-iteration builders (`_build_wp_iteration_decision`, `_map_wp_step_decision`) and the DAG-advance path route through one new board-authority selector (`_resolve_wp_board_action` in `runtime_bridge.py`) that resolves the same coord-aware `status_dir`/task-board `read_dir` via `mission_context_for` and consults the same `_finalized_task_board_override_step` + `preview_claimable_wp` authority query mode uses — so a rejected WP now re-dispatches `implement <wp>` on every topology (including the combined coord × review-reject cell), and coord/`lanes_with_coord` implement dispatch now succeeds. A board `blocked:*` sentinel (no actionable WP, all `in_review`, or an unmaterialized coordination surface) now surfaces as `kind=blocked` with a runnable named `spec-kitty` recovery command — never the WP-less placeholder and never a silent no-op. The approve control, the early-reject-while-on-`implement` control, and `single_branch`/`lanes` implement dispatch are unchanged; no persisted run/engine-state write is performed (the re-dispatch decision is recomputed from the board each call, verified by snapshot byte-identity before/after).
- **`spec-kitty agent tracer-append` and the decision ledger no longer silently destroy or hide a teammate's mission files when the coordination worktree isn't materialised — a fresh clone, a CI runner, or a removed worktree** (mission; `#4959`, `#4966`). **Before:** on a coord-topology mission from such a checkout, a coordination read fell through to an *empty* document and the command committed that empty default over the branch's real file at exit 0 — `tracer-append` overwrote a populated `traces/<category>.md` with a from-scratch header (every earlier finding lost), and the decision ledger resolved to a status-only husk so `decision open` returned `MISSION_NOT_FOUND` and `accept` could stay permanently blocked on a clarification marker with no CLI way out. **After:** the placement read seam **fails closed** — it raises a typed error that names how to materialise the worktree, instead of returning an empty document on an unmaterialised coordination surface; `tracer-append` refuses (leaving the real file byte-intact, and also refuses an undecodable file) rather than clobbering; and the decision ledger and `accept` now read the *same* authoritative copy, so a resolved decision is visible to `accept` and a mission can no longer get stuck. `spec-kitty merge`, another reader of that seam, now aborts before any state change with the same *materialise-the-worktree* remedy instead of dying with a raw traceback when it hits an unmaterialised coordination worktree. Part of the coord-husk fail-closed epic (`#5002`; the doctor-flatten sibling `#4979` remains open; the decision-ledger dual-partition reconciliation is tracked separately as `#5023`).
- **A repeated `spec-kitty upgrade` on an already-current project no longer wedges every in-flight coordination mission by stamping live worktrees with divergent metadata** (#4972). **Before:** when the CLI was already at the target version, `_upgrade_worktrees` still advanced each live worktree's `version` to the target and minted a **fresh `last_upgraded_at = now_utc()`** — a distinct timestamp per worktree — then auto-committed it on that worktree's own branch. `main`, the coordination branch, and each lane branch ended with three different values on that one bookkeeping line of `.kittify/metadata.yaml`, so `spec-kitty implement WP##` failed the dependency-lane auto-merge and `spec-kitty merge` refused the lane as stale — on `.kittify/metadata.yaml` alone — while both upgrade runs exited 0 "already up to date". A teammate who merely pulled an already-upgraded `main` (so `current_version == target_version`) hit it on their **first** `upgrade`. **After:** when a worktree's write is driven **solely** by the version bookkeeping bump — no migration applied real content, no metadata freshly synthesized — its `last_upgraded_at` is aligned to the main checkout's already-stored value instead of a fresh `now_utc()` — or, when main itself carries no stamp yet (a project init'd already at the target and never upgraded), to a single fallback timestamp minted once per run and shared by every sibling worktree, so siblings never diverge on their own `now_utc()` in that edge either. On this bookkeeping-only path `.kittify/metadata.yaml` then ends identical across `main`/coord/lane and 3-way-merges cleanly; a genuine content migration still stamps each worktree with a fresh `now_utc()` by design (no #2385 regression), and the existing churn-gate naturally suppresses the now-empty no-op commit. The fix lives at the single shared mint site (`_upgrade_worktrees`), so all three callers inherit it. Extends the #1838 no-op save-gate. Red-first `@pytest.mark.regression` coverage pins the divergence, the sibling-share fallback edge, and the #2385 + teammate-first-run guards. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **`spec-kitty doctor mission-state --fix` no longer silently discards an authoritative mission record whose event type a newer subsystem added before it was registered** (mission; `#4993`). **Before:** the repair preserved only a hard-coded allowlist of non-lane event types and quarantined everything else, so a record the running tool already treats as real (any row carrying an `event_type`) was dropped by `--fix` while it still reported exit-0 "success" — the same silent-loss shape as the acute `#4897` bug, now latent for any future record type. **After:** the repair preserves exactly what the durable reader preserves (pruning only an explicit, currently-empty denylist), and its fail-closed guard now errors instead of dropping any reader-preserved row. Two adjacent hardenings ride along: the project's configured mission type is now read through a single shared parser (removing a two-reader edge-case drift risk), and the `traces/` merge helper correctly handles `~~~` code fences and repeated section headings so no trace section is lost or mis-merged.
- **Terminus integrity follow-ups — the DEFAULT `spec-kitty merge` now enforces the tree-authoritative content guarantee, and a resumed merge no longer downgrades strategy or loses committed work (Epic #5001, completing the PR #5012 follow-ups).** **Before:** the reconciliation gate's content/excluded/closed-world checks only ran under `--strategy merge`; the DEFAULT squash `spec-kitty merge` early-returned PASS before them, so a removed/canceled WP's code could ride a carrier lane onto the target at exit 0 on the common default path (#5013, and #4945/#4977/#4981 for the default flow). `merge --resume` silently downgraded to squash (the operator's `--strategy` was never persisted or read back) and re-anchored its reconciliation claim to the resume-start coordination checkpoint — which already contained attempt-1's partial consolidation — so an already-merged lane's pre-interrupt commit was judged vacuously satisfied and dropped (#4982 #4997), and a non-default-target resume was blocked (#4985 #4991). The coordination write gate treated an unmaterialized local-head coord branch already carrying committed issue-matrix rows as a first-write self-materialization window and clobbered them, while `issue-verdict` resolved its write surface through the degrading read resolver (#4970). **After:** the default squash merge runs a squash-sound **blob-attribution content axis** — every non-bookkeeping content path of the squashed diff is attributed against the union of approved lanes' *first-parent authored blobs* (content identity, not lane-tip SHAs/patch-ids, which squash destroys); an unattributable path FAILs the gate and compare-and-swap-reverts the target (git-probe errors, an unresolved window base, and an empty authored set all REFUSE fail-closed, never PASS vacuously). `merge --resume` honors the persisted `MergeState.strategy` (and REFUSEs a contradictory explicit `--strategy`), and anchors the reconciliation claim to a read-persisted-first pre-mutation coordination base plus per-lane pre-interrupt tips (never the poisoned resume-start checkpoint), so an already-merged lane's exact commit is preserved by SHA on resume; the per-lane tip is a compare-and-swap expectation that tolerates the behind-HEAD window but REFUSEs true divergence. The coordination write gate refuses self-materialization when the local-head coord branch already carries committed matrix content (path derived from the placement authority so a drifted path is never read as absent), and `issue-verdict` routes through the fail-closed write resolver. Closes #5013, #4945, #4977, #4981 (default flow), #4970, #4985, #4991, #4982 with real-CLI red-first reproductions. Residual tracked follow-ups (honest `xfail(strict)`, not green-washed): **#4997** (resume SHA-preservation over the staged-deletion / `LOCAL_CHANGES` behind-HEAD window — a distinct window from #4982) and the 3-way merge-resolution content case (a target blob equal to neither parent). Sibling missions retain #4990 (reducer LWW) and #4972 (upgrade stamping).
- **Terminus/merge-coord integrity — a terminus command no longer exits 0 while destroying committed work or landing the wrong tree (Epic #5001).** **Before:** an ordinary `spec-kitty merge` / `merge --resume` could delete lanes, mark WPs `done`, and exit 0 while the target tree diverged from what the WP status/manifest claimed — the forward `update-ref` was a non-atomic 2-arg write guarded only by a TOCTOU ancestry precheck (removed/canceled code could ride a carrier lane onto the target); coordination teardown ran without projecting concurrent post-checkpoint status/verdict commits (they survived only in `fsck --unreachable`); a crashed `merge --target develop` resumed onto meta's `main`; `merge --abort` freed another live merge's global lock; a lanes/single_branch merge could `reset --hard` dirty planning artifacts as if they were coordination residue. **After:** a fail-closed **reconciliation gate** runs before any teardown — every approved WP's approved commits must be reachable from the target and nothing excluded may be, membership sourced through the Lamport reducer wrapper (never the LWW path) and approved SHAs read from lane-branch tips, with a closed-world check that FAILs (and compare-and-swap-reverts the target) on any un-attributable content commit. The forward ref advance is now real 3-arg compare-and-swap (no fallback/retry); coordination teardown projects all post-checkpoint commits and is CAS-gated; the strand heal reverts only recorded SHAs; the merge target is a single persisted authority (`--target` > persisted > meta) honored across resume; the merge lock carries an owner token so `--abort` frees only its own lock; the residue classifier is topology-aware; lane identity is stable and origin-aware; the behind-HEAD resume remedy no longer advises a merge-reverting commit. Docs corrected (forward advance is CAS; merge membership is Lamport-sourced). Ships 7 of the 12 child defects closed with real-CLI red-first reproductions (#4945 #4969 #4973 #4977 #4978 #4981 #4996); the default `squash` strategy enforces claim-integrity and reports honestly (content reachability deferred) rather than fabricating success. Tracked follow-ups: resume-strategy/SHA-preservation (#4982 #4997 #4985 #4991), surface-write self-materialization hardening (#4970), and squash-content-soundness. Sibling missions retain #4990 (reducer LWW) and #4972 (upgrade stamping).
- **`spec-kitty doctor coordination --fix` no longer fast-forwards the wrong branch and reports success when the coordination worktree has some other branch checked out** (#4950; fixes #4920). **Before:** the fix ran `git merge --ff-only <target>` inside the recorded coordination worktree without checking which branch it was on. If someone had checked out another branch there (for example a `qa-inspect` branch cut to look at something) or left it on a detached HEAD, `--fix` fast-forwarded *that* branch, left the coordination branch as stale as before, printed `Fast-forwarded: coordination branch '…'` and exited 0. Every rerun did the same thing again, while the same command's read-only pass was already warning `COORDINATION_WORKTREE_BRANCH_MISMATCH`. **After:** `--fix` checks the worktree first and refuses before touching anything when it is on another branch, detached, or not a worktree of this repository at all. The refusal uses the existing `COORDINATION_BRANCH_STALE_FIX_BLOCKED` error and exits 1, the same way `--fix` already refuses a diverged or dirty coordination branch. After a fast-forward it re-reads the coordination branch and prints `Fast-forwarded` only once that branch really matches the target; if it does not, `--fix` reports the new `COORDINATION_BRANCH_STALE_FIX_POSTCONDITION_FAILED` error instead of claiming success. A fast-forward that git itself rejects is now reported as a finding rather than crashing the run, so other missions in the same `--fix` run are still repaired. The strand repair in the same command (and in `spec-kitty merge`), which reverts a stranded `done` commit after a rolled-back merge, had the same blind spot: on a wrong branch it reverted there, reported the strand healed and stopped reporting it. It now refuses too and keeps the strand reported until it is really repaired. Red-first real-Git coverage pins each refusal and the success postcondition.
- **The overwrite / destination-clobber half of the asset-loss class is now closed by construction — a new non-vacuous overwrite ownership-routing census** (#4901). The removal census (`tests/architectural/test_mutation_ownership_routing.py`) deliberately excludes the overwrite family (`os.replace`/`os.rename`/`os.renames`/`Path.replace`) and explicitly defers it to #4901; the `guard_destructive_overwrite`/`OverwriteVerdict` primitive shipped and `research` and `write_mission_brief` route through it, but nothing *gated* that routing — a future destination-clobbering overwrite of operator content (a raw `os.replace`/`shutil.copy2` onto a user path, or a deleted guard call) would pass CI green, the exact class the removal census closes for its half. **After:** a separate `tests/architectural/test_overwrite_ownership_routing.py` gate (two seams stay separate) censuses the overwrite/copy-clobber class over the narrow mutating-flow scan set (`cli/commands/research.py`, `mission_brief.py`, `intake/brief_writer.py`) with BOTH non-vacuity mechanisms: a **positive-routing pin** (both consumers asserted, AST `ast.Call`, to call `guard_destructive_overwrite`; deleting either call reds the gate even though the surviving allowlisted `copy2` literal keeps a literal-only scan green) and a **copy-verb classifier** (rename family plus `shutil.copy2`/`copy`/`copyfile`, `Path.write_text`/`write_bytes`/`touch`, arity-guarded so `str.replace(a, b)` never matches, with a reference/exhaustiveness self-check). The atomic write-then-replace-own-tempfile idiom (`brief_writer.py`) and `research`'s guarded post-clear `copy2` are exempted per-site, never by module name. Reuses `tests/architectural/_destructive_op_census.py` read-only; the removal census is unchanged. Bug-fix (gate coverage); no CLI version bump.
- **Six architectural/performance test-guards now fail on the broken input they exist to catch (non-vacuity hardening)** (#4036, #4105, #4210, #4388, #4408, #4536; epic #4883). **Before:** each guard stayed green even when its target defect was present — the dead-src-path gate scanned `doc_status` over the whole file, so a body-prose `doc_status:` line vacuously skipped a page and hid a dead `src/…` literal (#4105); the performance-marker guard only parsed planted text and never AST-walked the real test tree (#4210); the CLI startup-budget scan had no minimum-scanned-file floor (a mis-rooted glob passed with zero offenders) and missed dynamic `importlib.import_module("jsonschema")`/`__import__` forms (#4536); `_gate_coverage._composite_action_path` resolved a `..`-traversal `uses:` to a path outside the actions tree (#4408); the module-shard `_PYTHON_FILE_PATTERNS` basis was not anchored against a `pytest.ini` `python_files` override (#4388); the repo-root status-guard self-check asserted absolute non-existence rather than its per-test window (#4036). **After:** each guard is tightened and carries a committed non-vacuity demonstration — RED on the planted broken input before the fix, GREEN after — so a future re-vacuation fails CI; **test-infra only, zero `src/` change**. The performance-marker real-tree walk is bounded (`rglob("test_*.py")` + `SyntaxError` catch + a rationale'd exemption list), its stale `pytest.ini` marker description is corrected, and a real invariant now asserts `SPEC_KITTY_RUN_PERFORMANCE` stays scoped to the nightly performance job. First mission-fixed slice of the deferred-squad-findings epic #4883.
- **`spec-kitty upgrade` is host-safe on Windows again: it no longer crashes applying managed skills, and a converged project no longer reports phantom repairs** (#4923, #4927; from the Windows verification report #4930). Windows filesystems cannot carry POSIX file modes, and the upgrade/skill-install surfaces were treating that as real state. **#4923 — Before:** every managed-skill write applied `os.utime`/`Path.chmod` with `follow_symlinks=False`; on Windows neither function is in `os.supports_follow_symlinks`, so the flag raised `NotImplementedError: utime: follow_symlinks unavailable on this platform` at `skills/installer.py`, aborting `spec-kitty upgrade` and leaving `.kittify/command-skills-manifest.json` partially applied (the released 4.0.0rc4 PyPI wheel is broken on this path). **After:** all five `follow_symlinks=False` chmod/utime sites route through two new host-safe primitives in `kernel.no_follow` (`utime_no_follow`/`chmod_no_follow`) that honor the flag only where the host lists the function in `os.supports_follow_symlinks` and fall back to a default-follow call otherwise — closing the class by construction, guarded by a non-vacuous, shrink-only architectural gate. POSIX symlink semantics are preserved where the host supports them. **#4927 — Before:** on a converged Windows project `upgrade --dry-run` reported `Would repair 184 supporting surface paths` (184 = one phantom `chmod` per managed file, because the Windows-observed mode never equals the planned POSIX mode) while `doctor tool-surfaces` reported the project clean — the two surfaces disagreed and the count never dropped. **After:** the host-aware mode-divergence relaxation (`windows_dir_mode_only_divergence`) is extended from directory-only to file/symlink kinds, so the project-skill projection emits no `chmod` effect whose sole divergence is a host-unrepresentable POSIX mode; a converged Windows project now reports zero supporting-surface repairs, agreeing with the auditor. Both fixes are strictly host-conditional — a genuine mode divergence on a real POSIX host still produces a repair — and are verified on Linux CI via the `kernel.paths.is_windows` seam with red-first repros that raise for the right reason pre-fix. #4925 (`upgrade --yes` exits 1 on a no-op) is deferred: it is untraced and cannot be faithfully reproduced on Linux; it may resolve downstream of #4927 and is tracked for Windows re-verification.
- **Seven mutating flows no longer silently overwrite, delete, or corrupt operator-authored files while reporting success — Spec Kitty stops fighting its own operator** (epic #4915; #4907, #4895, #4910, #2691, #4896, #4890, #4888). Each command below detected user content only by name/extension (or not at all) and mutated it with `exit 0`, no backup, and no warning — several targeting gitignored or untracked paths where the loss was unrecoverable. This extends the reach of the #4859/#4861/#4862 asset-preservation guard (which covered `init` + migrations) to the remaining flows, and applies the charter's User Customization Preservation invariant uniformly. All fixes are ATDD red-first (an issue-pinned `@pytest.mark.regression` reproduction that was RED on the mission base and GREEN on the fix). No CLI version bump — these are bug fixes.
  - **`agent config remove <agent>` / `agent config sync` no longer delete user-authored command surfaces** (#4907, P0; #2691). `_remove_project_agent_surface` ran an unconditional `shutil.rmtree` on an agent's managed subdir (e.g. `.claude/commands/**` — in 4.x purely user-owned and gitignored, so unrecoverable) for both the explicit `remove` verb and `sync`'s default-on orphan sweep. **After:** the removal routes through the shared `asset_preservation.guard_destructive_removal` with a content-based `ManifestProver` at directory granularity — a surface whose ownership cannot be proven is preserved whole (never a partial `rmtree` on a mixed manifest+user directory) and reported as *preserved*, exit 0; a genuinely manifest-proven surface is still removed. Messaging is now verdict-driven, so a preserved surface can never be falsely reported as "Removed" (#4907's `root.rmdir()`-OSError-swallow bug). Separately, a normal `sync` no longer rewrites a repository-pinned `command-skills-manifest.json` (#2691's second half): the already-installed skill-agent registration is skipped, pinned release/hash values stay byte-identical, and `sync --json` enumerates the tracked mutations (zero on a non-refreshing sync).
  - **`implement` no longer clobbers a repository's own `.git/hooks/pre-commit`** (#4895, P0). The hook installer `os.replace`'d the guard hook over any existing hook with no check, silently disabling the operator's commit-time checks for **every** commit repo-wide (`.git/hooks` is shared across worktrees), untracked and unrecoverable. **After:** a foreign hook (one not bearing the `# Generated by spec-kitty.` signature, mirroring the retirement migration's ownership proof) is backed up to a timestamped sidecar via a new shared symlink-aware `asset_preservation.backup.backup_before_overwrite` helper before install, and the backup path is surfaced in `implement`'s output; a spec-kitty-signed hook is replaced as before.
  - **`intake` no longer overwrites a hand-authored `.kittify/mission-brief.md`** (#4910). The overwrite gate keyed on the *conjunction* of the brief and its provenance sidecar existing, so a hand-written brief with no sidecar (the most natural shape) was silently replaced. **After:** the gate keys on the brief's existence alone at both entry points (explicit and `--auto`) — a missing sidecar is treated as unknown provenance and the command refuses without `--force`, leaving the brief byte-identical.
  - **`validate-encoding --fix` no longer corrupts the files it claims to repair** (#4896). A single stray byte triggered a whole-file cp1252 re-decode that mojibaked every multi-byte character; binaries named `*.md` were rewritten; and CRLF was converted to LF file-wide — all reported `Fixed`, exit 0, on a command the shipped `AGENTS.md` tells agents to run routinely. **After:** text vs binary is classified by content sniff (never extension), so binaries are skipped; the fallback decode is scoped to the offending byte(s) or the file is refused with the offending offset(s) — never a whole-file transcode; existing line endings are preserved; and "Fixed" is reported only on a faithful repair.
  - **The legacy `agent tasks finalize-tasks` no longer wedges a mission with a false-success dependency graph** (#4890). It validated the graph parsed from `tasks.md` but persisted the WP *frontmatter* dependencies unvalidated, so a cycle / self-reference / unknown-WP reference living only in frontmatter finalized with exit 0, a falsified `dependencies` payload, and seeded status — leaving both WPs permanently unclaimable. **After:** it validates the *effective persisted* graph with the same validator the canonical `agent mission finalize-tasks` uses (cycle detection + `validate_dependencies`); on any violation it exits non-zero and seeds no status, and on success the `dependencies` payload equals the graph actually written.
  - **`safe_commit` no longer wipes the operator's staged work, and `upgrade` no longer hides it** (#4888). Every Spec Kitty auto-commit preserved unrelated staged changes with `git stash push --staged` / `git stash pop --index`, which deterministically fails whenever any unrelated tracked file is partially staged (an everyday `git add -p` state) — stranding the operator's staged work in an un-poppable stash; `upgrade` then swallowed the typed signal and exited 0 with "please commit manually" (the commit had already landed), never naming the stash. **After:** `safe_commit` commits exactly the requested paths via `git commit --only`, never touching the operator's index or working tree; when a residual restore path does fail, `upgrade` propagates the typed `SafeCommitRecoveryFailed` (naming the stash ref and the landed commit SHA) and exits non-zero instead of a misleading success.
  - **Closed by construction:** the mutation-ownership routing gate (`tests/architectural/test_mutation_ownership_routing.py`) is widened to census `agent config`'s removal surface, so a future un-routed destructive removal there fails the gate rather than silently reintroducing the data-loss class.
- **`spec-kitty init` no longer silently deletes an operator-authored `.kittify/templates/` tree — the sibling residual of the #4861 guard fix** (#4931). **Before:** on a project with no `.kittify/config.yaml`, `init` proved `.kittify/templates` package-owned by its path NAME (`ManagedPathProver(managed_relpaths={".kittify/templates", …})`), so the #4861 removal guard deleted a user-authored resolver LEGACY tier with no backup — exit 0, `Project ready` — and the full-copy template path (`template/manager.py`) `rmtree`'d it unguarded in BOTH the `--local` and the pip-default package modes. **After:** the cleanup guard proves the templates dir owned only by this-invocation `run_created` provenance (never by name, per charter §470), and that provenance is now gated on the copy step *actually creating* the tree (both copy functions return a `TemplateCopyResult.templates_created` signal, set only inside their own source-exists guard) — so a pre-existing tree is preserved (or archived to `.kittify/.backup-<ts>/`) with the same "not package-owned — left in place" diagnostic `command-templates` already prints, INCLUDING the source-absent path (partial checkout / relocated source) that would otherwise re-arm the deletion; both full-copy functions (`copy_specify_base_from_local` and the pip-installed-default `copy_specify_base_from_package`) back up any pre-existing `templates/` before overwrite via the in-file `back_up_operator_subtrees` precedent (#4759). Red-first CLI/functional coverage drives the real `init` over the guard path, both full-copy paths (the package path exercised directly), and the source-absent case, plus controls proving a genuinely run-created tree is still cleaned. Bug-fix; no CLI version bump.
- **`spec-kitty research` no longer fabricates 0-byte "ready" artifacts when no template resolves, and `--force` no longer truncates a user-authored research artifact to empty** (#4926). **Before:** on a `software-dev` mission (which ships no research templates), `research` `touch`ed four 0-byte files (`research.md`, `data-model.md`, `research/evidence-log.csv`, `research/source-register.csv`), rendered the green "N artifacts ready" panel, and exited 0; with `--force` over an existing user-authored artifact it `unlink`ed then `touch`ed, truncating it to zero bytes. **After:** every asset routes through the shared `guard_destructive_overwrite` primitive (`replacement_substantive` = a template actually resolved, `authorized` = `--force`); a non-substantive write never proceeds — no fabrication, and `--force` never truncates to empty — the skip decision is taken before any filesystem mutation, the created/success panel reflects only real writes, and the outcome is reported honestly from each asset's skip reason (a genuine no-template run says "no research template for mission type X"; a plain re-run whose templates resolve but whose files already exist says "existing artifacts preserved; re-run with --force"). The architectural gate `test_mutation_ownership_routing` now scans `research.py` (its raw removal literals are routed away, never allowlisted). Red-first CLI coverage drives the real `research` command over all four assets for the fabrication, the `--force`-truncation, and the honest-re-run-reporting cases.
- **The mission-brief overwrite invariant now lives in the `write_mission_brief` chokepoint, not only the `intake` CLI adapter — so no future writer-layer caller can silently clobber a hand-authored brief** (#4921; durable architecture follow-up to #4910/#4918). **Before:** the "refuse to overwrite an existing brief without `--force`" guard existed only in the two duplicated `intake.py` CLI gates; the exported `write_mission_brief` writer overwrote unconditionally (its only existence logic was the partial-state XOR recovery), so any other caller reintroduced the #4910 loss one layer down. **After:** `write_mission_brief(overwrite=False)` raises a typed `BriefExistsError` when a brief already exists — keyed on the brief's existence alone (a brief-only, sidecar-absent file is unknown-provenance and still refused) and evaluated BEFORE the partial-state XOR cleanup, so a brief-only file is never unlink-then-rewritten. The two `intake` gates and the `--auto` path delegate to the chokepoint (catching the typed error → the existing `--force` message), collapsing the duplication; the orphan-sidecar (brief-absent) recovery path is unchanged. The shared `guard_destructive_overwrite` primitive it uses is the same one #4926 consumes — one preservation authority for the overwrite/truncate seam, beside the landed `guard_destructive_removal`. Red-first coverage witnesses the writer-layer destroyer on the base and pins the brief-only refusal.
- **`spec-kitty charter activate` / `deactivate` / `pack apply --compile` on a non-`software-dev` project no longer silently rewrite the compiled charter's mission type to `software-dev` and drop its references** (#4908). The post-activation catalog recompile is a derived-view writer (it rebuilds `catalog.references`) that fabricated an input it should have read from the source of truth. **Before:** on a project generated with `--mission-type research`, a single routine `charter activate directive <id>` recompiled `.kittify/charter/charter.yaml` with `catalog.mission` flipped `research → software-dev`, `catalog.template_set` flipped `research-default → software-dev-default`, and `catalog.references` dropped from 268 to 165 ids — exit 0, no mission-change notice, no backup. The recompile path called the generate loader with `from_interview=False, resolved_mission_type=None`, so with the interview deliberately not loaded (the #2940 malformed-answers guard) the mission collapsed to the `"software-dev"` literal, discarding the project's recorded type. The compiled charter is the canonical governance catalog read by `charter context`, the runtime prompt builder, and the dispatch router, so every downstream action was then mis-governed. **After:** the recompile fallback reads the recorded mission from its SSOT — `charter.yaml` `catalog.mission` (guaranteed present at the activate recompile guard), then `answers.yaml` `mission:` — before falling back to `"software-dev"` only when neither exists; one seam fixes `activate`, `deactivate`, and `pack apply --compile`. The #2940 guard is preserved (`from_interview` is never flipped, so a malformed `answers.yaml` still degrades to `None` without aborting). Red-first `@pytest.mark.regression` coverage drives the real `charter generate` + `charter activate` CLI and isolates the mission-flip from the orthogonal FR-018 config-narrowing. This is a bug-fix — no CLI version bump.
- **`spec-kitty doctor mission-state --fix` (and `spec-kitty upgrade`) no longer quarantine a healthy mission's authoritative Decision-Moment rows while reporting `errors=0`** (#4897). Two subsystems disagreed about who owns `DecisionPoint*` rows in the shared `status.events.jsonl` append log. **Before:** the decisions subsystem treats that log as authoritative and `decisions/index.json` as a derived fold, but the mission-state repair's `_is_preserved_non_lane_row` kept a hand-narrowed preserved-set (retrospective + `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_TYPES` only) on the inverted premise that `DecisionPoint*` rows were "a prunable mirror". So `--fix` on a healthy mission with a recorded Decision Moment removed both `DecisionPointOpened`/`DecisionPointResolved` rows, exited 0 with `errors=0`, and the advertised follow-up `doctor decisions --repair` then rebuilt the index from the emptied log to zero entries — the question, options, chosen answer, rationale, resolver, and idempotency key became unreadable by every CLI surface. **After:** a single authoritative-non-lane-event-type registry (`AUTHORITATIVE_NON_LANE_EVENT_TYPES` in `status/lifecycle_events.py`) is the one source both the durable reader (`status/store.py::is_non_lane_event`) and the repair (`_is_preserved_non_lane_row`) consult, closing the recurring whack-a-field class (#2376 retrospective, #3066 `WPStatusChanged`, #3541 `review_result`, now #4897 `DecisionPoint`) by construction rather than by adding another hand-maintained entry; already-preserved classes are unchanged (the registry is a strict superset). A fail-closed guard makes a repair that would quarantine a registry-authoritative row report an error instead of a silent `errors=0` success. Red-first `@pytest.mark.regression` coverage drives the real `repair_repo` / decisions-service path and witnesses the silent quarantine (not the #2376 all-dropped backstop). Bug-fix — no CLI version bump.
- **`spec-kitty doctor mission-state --fix` now keeps a durable, operator-visible audit trail — its repair manifest and quarantined rows survive `git clean` instead of vanishing** (#4928; the placement/durability follow-up to #4897). **Before:** the per-run manifest and the verbatim quarantine of any removed rows were written under the gitignored `.kittify/migrations/mission-state/`, so `git clean -xfd` destroyed the only record of a destructive repair and nothing in the `--fix` output warned the operator the artifacts were untracked — a defence-in-depth gap that became real loss for anyone cleaning their tree after a repair. That placement was itself a deliberate #2384 decision (ignore the trail so a repair does not dirty the tree or gate `accept`). **After:** the manifest and quarantine relocate to the git-TRACKED `.kittify/mission-state-audit/`, so the trail survives `git clean` once committed; the #2384 non-gating property is preserved by classifying the tracked root as self-bookkeeping churn (a `--fix` run still never gates `accept`/`merge`/`record-analysis`) rather than by ignoring it; and `--fix` now prints a write-only exit summary naming the manifest (always) and the quarantine path + row count (when rows were moved), marked tracked-but-uncommitted with a commit instruction (`--json` carries the same paths + count). The canonical state contract (`migration_state_ledger`) becomes `TRACKED` and a new `legacy_migration_scratch` surface keeps the old `.kittify/migrations/` ignore for back-compat; the three architectural archive ratchets are repointed to the new quarantine path (kept excluded — verbatim historical rows), while the manifest is ordinary reviewable content. A real-git-repo durability e2e exercises BOTH repair writers end-to-end (check-ignore clean → `git add` stages → survives `git clean` → self-bookkeeping-churn non-gating). No row-canonicality change (the #4897 registry is untouched). Bug-fix — no CLI version bump.
- **The `spec-kitty-traces` git merge driver no longer silently deletes repeated lines (code fences, headings, repeated prose) from `traces/*.md` on an ordinary merge** (#4894). `init` binds `kitty-specs/**/traces/*.md` to a custom merge driver that resolves *every* ordinary `git merge`/`rebase`/`cherry-pick` touching a traces file, not only spec-kitty's own squash. **Before:** its `union_trace_texts` walked ours then theirs with one shared line-level `seen` set and dropped every non-empty line already emitted — so markdown's legitimately-recurring lines (```` ``` ```` fences, `Example:`, `---`, table separators, repeated headings) were deleted after their first occurrence, collapsing a document with four fenced blocks to one fence line and swallowing the rest into an unterminated code block, while `git merge` printed `Auto-merging …`, exited 0, and recorded a clean merge. **After:** the driver unions at markdown-section/block granularity (fence-aware boundary detection), deduping only whole byte-identical sections and preserving repeated lines within distinct sections, and it now reads `%O` for 3-way base-awareness (a theirs section unchanged-from-base while ours edited it is superseded; a genuinely-new theirs section is kept; a both-sides-divergent section keeps both copies — never a silent lossy exit-0). The invariant: no non-empty line present in either input is absent from the output, or the merge conflicts. The sibling `_union_acceptance_history` record-granularity dedup is untouched. Red-first `@pytest.mark.regression` coverage drives a real `git merge` through a worktree-src shim (immune to the stale editable install). Bug-fix — no CLI version bump.
- **Default squash integration no longer silently reverts newer target-branch source changes** (#4892). `spec-kitty merge` previously ran `git merge --squash -X theirs`, so an ordinary same-hunk source conflict was auto-resolved in the mission's favour, reported success, and proceeded to work-package finalization and lane cleanup. Squash integration now uses normal three-way semantics and fails closed on unresolved ordinary content before committing or advancing the target ref; disjoint edits still combine, registered artifact merge drivers remain path-scoped authorities, and target-newer planning artifacts retain their existing history-aware reconciliation. `spec-kitty merge --dry-run` exercises the same isolated squash primitive and emits `TARGET_BRANCH_CONTENT_CONFLICT` with deterministic paths and remediation, while the clean success payload stays unchanged. The fix also holds under `spec-kitty merge --resume` (a conflict whose path happened to contain "already" could previously be mistaken for an "already merged" branch and slip through to done-marking and cleanup — the conflict is now carried as structured data and always fails closed), the real merge prints the same `TARGET_BRANCH_CONTENT_CONFLICT` code and remediation the dry-run does, a conflict that resolves entirely to the target is reported as a no-op instead of a fabricated empty squash commit, and a non-conflict `--dry-run` preview failure now returns a valid JSON error instead of a traceback.
- **A project-layer agent profile's cited directives, tactics, and styleguide pointers now render in the dispatch capsule / governance context even when the repository declares no organization packs** (#4912; #4838). **Before:** in a project with no org packs, invoking `--profile <id>` on a profile authored under `.kittify/doctrine/agent_profiles/` printed `WARNING  Profile '<id>' not found; profile-cited sections omitted` and dropped every profile-cited section — even though the same profile's header, governance context, and model routing all rendered fine. The charter profile-cited resolver took a built-in-only fast path whenever no org packs were declared, and a project-authored profile lives only in the activation-aware catalog, so it was never found. **After:** any caller with a repository root resolves through the activation-aware profile map (project + org + built-in), so a project profile's citations render; the built-in-only bootstrap path is kept only for callers with no repository root at all. Activation is now honored without org packs too, uniformly with org-pack repos: an explicitly de-activated profile — project **or** built-in — has its profile-cited sections omitted from the capsule (a fail-closed change from the old ungated no-org-packs fast path; the common case of no `activated_agent_profiles` allowlist is unchanged). This is the charter-context sibling of #4114/#4128, which closed the same built-in-only drop in the dispatch router catalog (a distinct seam); no migration required.
